title: This clock yells if you read it wrong 😤 Telling time in Korean #learnkorean
caption:
Korean has two sets of numbers, and a clock uses both.

Hours use the 하나 · 둘 · 셋 set → 한 시, 두 시, 세 시
Minutes use the 일 · 이 · 삼 set → 십 분 (10), 이십 분 (2 × 10), 삼십 분 (3 × 10)

3:30 = 세 시 삼십 분 (se si sam-sip bun)
10:15 = 열 시 십오 분 (yeol si sip-o bun)

Not 삼 시.
You can also say 세 시 반 (se si ban) for 3:30 — 반 means half.

pinnedComment: What time is it for you right now? Say it in Korean 👇
alt: A needle-felted study corner with a big round wall clock showing 3:30. A coral felt mascot reads it as 삼 시 삼십 분…? The short orange clock hand, with a round angry felt face, jumps out and shouts 세 시! The mascot wonders 세…? 삼…? and the long blue hand shouts 삼십 분! The two hands yell 세! and 삼십! at each other louder and louder until their heads crash and the mascot is pushed aside. 3 is both 세 and 삼: Korean has two sets of numbers. The short hand ticks through 한 시, 두 시, 세 시 and the long hand through 십 분, 이십 분, 삼십 분. The mascot reads 세 시 삼십 분 and a chime rings. The hands spin to 10:15 and glare; the trembling mascot whispers 열 시… 십오 분…? and the chime rings again. It puffs up and shouts 열 시 십오 분! and the two hands flinch, meek and shrunken. Hours 한 · 두 · 세, minutes 일 · 이 · 삼.
